column2: ...A little more...
a little farther up...
I was thinking those improper thoughts when it happened.
“Kyaa!”
Damn,
she noticed...
I thought, but that didn't seem to be it.
{n2} had a hand over her mouth and was staring wide-eyed at the window.
“The window...
outside the window...!”
“Outside the window?”
I turned my face, but nothing could be seen from the dark window.
“What about the window?”
“Someone was watching!”
“Huh?
This is the second floor, you know?”
Thinking it couldn't be, I stood and went over to the window.
{n2} stayed pale, not even moving from the bed.
I pressed my nose to the glass and peered into the darkness outside.
All I could tell was that snow was dancing in the light from the room.
I made up my mind and opened the window.
I stuck my head out into the madly whirling blizzard and looked all around.
“I don't see anything!”
To avoid catching a cold, I quickly shut the window and brushed off the snow that had fallen on my head and shoulders.
“I'm not lying!
Someone was peeking in!”
{n2} insisted, getting worked up.
I said with a laugh.
“It must be a ghost.”
“Honestly!
You never take me seriously!”
“Probably an optical illusion...”
What I wanted to say was, 'Anyway, about continuing that massage...'
but {n2} seemed to be in no mood for that at all.
“Maybe a spy is lurking around?”
“Huh?”
For an instant, {n2}'s eyes seemed to flash...
or was that just an illusion?
She quickly returned to her usual expression and said:
“...Something feels creepy. Want to go downstairs?”
“Y-yeah...
sure.”
The night is long, I thought.
In the lounge downstairs, sofas were arranged around a large brown table.
We decided to sit there and wait until dinner began.
Near the front desk, three girls were shouting something at Mr. Kobayashi.
“Now, now.
Please calm down and tell me.{r}{p}What on earth happened?”
“From the window, someone...
someone was peeking in!”
The moment we heard that, {n2} and I looked at each other.
Mr. Kobayashi gave a stiff laugh and said:
“Th-
that can't be.{r}{p}In this blizzard,
and on the second floor? Maybe you mistook a tree branch or something.”
“I didn't mistake anything!
There was a person outside the window.”
As if backing up the glasses girl who kept insisting, {n2} spoke up too.
“Uncle...
I saw it too.
In {n1}'s room.{r}{p}They said it was an illusion and I thought maybe so for a moment, but...”
“Hey, hey.
Now {n2}, too? What are you saying?{r}{p}You thought it might be an illusion, didn't you?
It's an illusion.”
Mr. Kobayashi laughed it off, but his eyes weren't smiling at all.
Something was off about Mr. Kobayashi's attitude.
So I thought, but the girls didn't seem to notice that much.
Looking creeped out, they gave up, backed off, and returned upstairs.
But {n2} wasn't convinced.
“Hey, Uncle.
It's strange for a mere illusion to happen to separate people at the same time.”
“...You must have mistaken the same thing.”
Mr. Kobayashi answered, eyes downcast.
“But {n1}'s room and theirs are on completely opposite sides, you know?{r}{p}If something you could mistake for a person
is circling around this place, that alone is creepy enough.”
Please, don't say that so loudly.”
Mr. Kobayashi lowered his voice in a fluster.
“This is a business. I can't have strange rumors going around.”
Saying so, he came over to the sofa where we sat.
He sat down knee to knee with us and began to speak in a whisper.
“...Listen.
Keep this between us.”
We swallowed hard and nodded.
“I want you to remember that I don't necessarily believe it, nor do I admit it, but...{r}{p}
what I mean is...
apparently, sometimes, something shows up.”
Mr. Kobayashi said, embarrassed.
“Shows up?
What does?”
{n2} asked blankly.
“The sort of thing you two saw.{r}{p}Don't ask me what it is.{r}{p}It's not like I've seen it myself.”
“A gh...
ghost?”
{n2} said in surprise, but Mr. Kobayashi neither denied nor confirmed it.
A strange silence fell.
{n2} and I searched each other's faces, unsure whether it was all right to laugh.
“Hey, Uncle.
Is this an elaborate joke to scare us?{r}{p}You never lose that mischievous streak...”
“Don't be silly!
If it were a joke, I'd keep it to you two.{r}{p}I wouldn't scare the other guests.”
That was true.
As he'd said earlier, the worst thing in the hospitality business is a bad reputation.
It didn't seem a prank worth taking such a risk for.
“Then...
then it really does show up?{r}{p}A ghost?
In this inn?”
Mr. Kobayashi didn't answer.
He probably didn't want to admit such a thing as a ghost.
“So several people have seen it before?”
When {n2} changed the question, Mr. Kobayashi nodded.
“Since when, exactly?”
“...The very first winter after I started this place, there were already complaints.{r}{p}Someone peeked in, they said.{r}{p}At first I assumed somebody really had peeked in, so
I went out to look around.{r}{p}But there wasn't a single footprint in the snow.{r}{p}Whatever they saw, it couldn't have been human.”
“Couldn't it be an animal?
A flying squirrel or a bat, some unfamiliar animal they mistook...”
“Then it would be strange for it to appear only in midwinter, wouldn't it?”
“It doesn't show up in other seasons?”
“Never.”
Mr. Kobayashi said firmly.
A midwinter ghost...
An image like a snow woman came to mind, and I shuddered.
But {n2} seemed to be a bit more rational.
“Isn't it a prank by someone with a vacation house nearby?{r}{p}Maybe it's their hobby, coming every year to scare the guests.”
“There's no house within walking distance, and if someone came by car, I couldn't fail to notice.
Listen, I've already thought through all those angles to death.
And the conclusion I came to is this...
forget it.”
{n2} wanted to keep talking, but Mr. Kobayashi stood up as if to say that's the end of it.
Just then, we noticed the sound of a car engine approaching.
“Huh?
Who on earth at this hour...”
“Ah, come to think of it, there's one guest who hasn't arrived yet.{r}{p}That's probably him.”
Mr. Kobayashi said, and slowly headed to the front desk.
The engine sound died as the car must have gone around to the parking lot.
Before long, a man covered in snow came in through the entrance.
“Sorry!
I'm late...”
“Mr. Mikimoto, is it?”
When Mr. Kobayashi called out from the front desk, the man nodded.
“Boy, was it rough!
I've never seen snow this bad.”
Saying so cheerfully, the man took off his shoes and filled out the register at the front desk.
“Dinner is already over, but I can prepare something like sandwiches, if you like?”
“No, no, that's fine.
Don't trouble yourself.”
He seemed an extremely cheerful man.
Spotting {n2} and me in the lounge, he left his luggage at the entrance and came over.
“Hi there.”
With a mountain-man's bearded face, he greeted us with a big smile.
“Hello.”
{n2} and I bowed our heads politely.
With that alone, the man acted as if we'd been friends for ten years, plopped down heavily on the sofa, and started talking to us.
“Say, you two, how long have you been here?”
“Since yesterday.”
“Hmm,
yesterday, huh...{r}{p}So, anything unusual happen?”
“Huh?
How do you know that?”
I asked back in surprise.
“So there was something, wasn't there?”
He leaned in eagerly.
“Well...
sort of...”
Since Mr. Kobayashi had told us to keep quiet, it was hard to say it outright.
Having caught our conversation, Mr. Kobayashi came flying over with a pale face.
“Excuse me, please don't.{r}{p}Nothing that inconveniences the other guests.”
“Inconvenience?
I only talked to them a little.{r}{p}Oh, I forgot to introduce myself, here is who I am.”
Saying so, he held out a business card.
On it was written 'Freelance Writer, Yosuke Mikimoto.'
“A freelance writer...
did you come here on assignment?”
Mr. Kobayashi said, sounding surprised.
“Well, yes.
I caught wind of a rumor, you see.”
“A rumor?
What kind of rumor?”
nothing much. Probably the sort of hoax spread by middle schoolers nearby.”
what kind of hoax?”
Mr. Kobayashi seemed to be trying not to show his agitation, but unfortunately it wasn't working.
“Don't laugh, now.{r}{p}It's a truly silly rumor.
...Ghosts.
They say this inn has a ghost.{r}{p}Funny, isn't it?”
Nobody laughed.
Seeing how we reacted, he seemed to grasp the situation.
“I see.
You saw it too, didn't you?{r}{p}Then it wasn't a hoax after all.”
Suddenly Mr. Kobayashi burst out in hysterical laughter.
“Not a hoax, you say?{r}{p}Do you actually believe in the existence of ghosts?”
“I don't believe either way, personally.{r}{p}I just introduce places where several people claim to have seen something as occult spots.
So, what about you?
You saw something, didn't you? What was it like?”
{n2} lowered her eyes in silence.
She probably meant it for her uncle's sake, but it was no use.
Because in the next moment, a woman's scream echoed through the entire inn.
Mr. Mikimoto was the first to dash off, ahead of everyone.
Mr. Kobayashi followed him.
Then {n2} and I chased after.
When we ran up to the second floor, one of the doors opened and a figure appeared.
It was Mr. Kayama.
“Ah, Kobayashi!
Good thing ya came.{r}{p}Haruko...
Haruko...”
“What's happened to your wife?”
Mr. Kobayashi stepped forward and asked.
Mr. Kayama didn't answer, only gesturing into the room with his hand.
Mr. Kobayashi peered in, gasped, and rushed inside.
We followed.
“Mrs. Kayama!”
Mr. Kobayashi ran to Haruko, lying on the floor, and lifted her up.
“What on earth happened?”
Mr. Mikimoto was asking Mr. Kayama.
“I dunno myself.{r}{p}She was lookin' toward the window, suddenly screamed, and collapsed.{r}{p}I looked outside too, but nothin' looked out of the ordinary...”
{n2} and I looked at each other.
“I knew it...”
Mr. Mikimoto muttered.
“You knew it?
What d'ya mean, ya knew it?”
Mr. Kayama asked back angrily, but Mr. Mikimoto didn't answer and asked a question instead.
“Isn't your wife someone with strong spiritual sensitivity?”
spiritual sensitivity?
What're ya talkin' about?”
“Well, is she?{r}{p}Doesn't she often get sleep paralysis, or hear sounds that you can't?”
“...Sleep paralysis, all the time.{r}{p}Especially when we go travelin'.{r}{p}She says it's 'cause she's got strong spiritual sensitivity, but if ya ask me, she just gets tired easy...”
“It seems that settles it.”
Mr. Mikimoto said to Mr. Kobayashi.
“Settles what?
What're ya sayin' ya figured out?”
Glancing at the dissatisfied Mr. Kayama, Mr. Mikimoto said:
“That there's something in this inn other than ourselves.”
I had the illusion that a gust of wind swept through us as we stood frozen.
It was Mr. Kobayashi who first broke the long silence.
“Don't be ridiculous!{r}{p}Mr. Kayama said so himself.
She tires easily, he said.{r}{p}Tired and dozing, she must have had a daydream.”
It seemed too late at night to call it a daydream, but I wanted to agree with Mr. Kobayashi too.
But Mr. Kayama cut in.
“No,
Haruko wasn't sleepin'.{r}{p}She was wide awake.”
“But, you see...”
Just as Mr. Kobayashi was about to retort, Haruko groaned and stirred.
Ohh...”
“Haruko!
Are ya all right?!”
Mr. Kayama lifted her up and shook her.
Shaking her head, Haruko opened her eyes and looked around.
dear...
I'm sorry.{r}{p}Did I faint?”
“Ya did.
Just for a little bit, though.”
“What exactly did you see?”
Mr. Mikimoto cut in from the side.
Haruko clapped a hand over her mouth, as if she'd remembered something terrifying.
“...Someone...
someone was staring at us from outside the window!{r}{p}Cold eyes glowing in the darkness...”
She closed her eyes and shook her head, as if trying to forget.
“What sort of person was it?”
Mr. Mikimoto asked further.
“What sort, you say...
only the eyes were glowing...
they were eerie eyes.”
“You can't even tell whether it was a man or a woman?”
I'm afraid not.”
A heavy silence took over the room again.
Eerie eyes glowing in the dark...
Could those really have been a human's?
did something happen?”
The girls were peering in from the hallway.
Mr. Kobayashi flew over to them and explained.
“It's nothing!
...It's nothing at all.{r}{p}Mrs. Kayama just isn't feeling very well.”
Pushing out the girls, who didn't look convinced, Mr. Kobayashi shut the door.
“...Now this is getting interesting.”
Mr. Mikimoto said, licking his lips.
“What's so interesting?!
This is no joking matter!”
Mr. Kobayashi glared sharply.
“I'm not treating it as a joke.{r}{p}I just think that this time it might be the real thing.”
“The real thing?
You mean a real ghost?{r}{p}A grown man saying such a thing...”
Mr. Mikimoto cut Mr. Kobayashi off and raised his voice.
“Twenty years ago, on Christmas Eve...
does anyone here know what happened in this place?”
That was when I saw Mr. Kobayashi's face turn white as paper.
“You...
just who are you?!”
“The owner surely knows.{r}{p}Anyone else?
No one?
Then let me tell you what I've been able to find out myself.”
“Don't...
don't listen to a thing this shady character says!”
“Yes,
understood.”
I covered my ears.
{n2} was saying something.
Mr. Kobayashi cut her off angrily.
I couldn't hear anything.
I couldn't stand it, and took my hands away.
In the next moment, at what Mr. Mikimoto said, {n2} and I both gasped.
“I think {n2} has a right to hear this.{r}{p}She's also a party to the incident.”
“A party...
to the incident?
Me?”
“Don't listen!
Mr. Kobayashi shouted, but I could sense a half-resigned tone in his voice.
“You haven't told her anything?
Nothing at all?{r}{p}Isn't that a bit too cruel?
Not even knowing what became of her own parents...”
Shock ran through {n2}'s face like an electric jolt.
“My own...
parents?
Mine?{r}{p}But I...
I...{r}{p}Uncle!
Is what this man is saying true?
Please, answer me!
My father and mother...”
Pressed by {n2}, Mr. Kobayashi lowered his eyes and turned his face away in anguish.
“...I'm sorry, {n2}.
We had no choice.
We had no choice...”
There was a moment of silence.
Eventually, Mr. Mikimoto lowered his tone and began to speak again.
“Twenty years ago, this wasn't a neat little inn like this, but a small charcoal-burner's hut.{r}{p}This whole area belonged to a certain big landowner,
and the one living in the charcoal hut was one of his many hired hands.”
“That landowner had three children.{r}{p}Two sons, Ichiro and Jiro, and a daughter, Junko.”
{n2}, startled, couldn't help cutting in.
“Junko...
my...
mother?{r}{p}But my mother only had one sibling, my uncle...”
Ignoring that voice, Mr. Mikimoto continued.

“The eldest son, Ichiro, defying his parents' opposition, was seeing the lovely only daughter of the couple living in the charcoal hut.{r}{p}But when the landowner learned that the girl, Miyuki, was carrying Ichiro's child,
he was said to have flown into a rage.”
{n2}'s face turned deathly pale.
{n2}'s uncle wasn't the eldest son, but had an older brother?
Considering that the uncle's name was Jiro, it was a very plausible story.
But could that Ichiro's child be...?
Mr. Mikimoto went on.

“As her due date approached, there was no sign of father and son reconciling, and Ichiro, half disowned, came to live in the charcoal hut.{r}{p}...And then, on a blizzard night like this, the kind when they say the
kamaitachi comes out, Ichiro was summoned by his father and given one last attempt at persuasion.”
“He had no intention of listening, of course, but his father, unusually, tried to keep his son there.
But noticing something odd in his father's behavior, he hurried his car to this hut.{r}{p}And what he found there was...”
Someone gulped audibly.
“Miyuki and her parents, lying in a sea of blood.”
As {n2} swayed unsteadily, I hurriedly supported her.
“All three had their throats slit and died almost instantly.{r}{p}But, astonishingly, one life was spared.{r}{p}The life of the unborn child, not yet nine months along at the time...”
Then Mr. Mikimoto stared straight at {n2}.
“That child, taken from the corpse's belly, was named {n2}, and was raised as the child of his younger sister Junko and her husband, who were known to be unable to have children...”
I looked at {n2}.
{n2} was looking at Mr. Kobayashi.
Mr. Kobayashi kept his eyes down, glaring at the floor.
Big tears welled in {n2}'s eyes and ran down her cheeks.
“...Is it true?
...Uncle,
was that story true?
Please, answer me!”
“The story isn't over yet, {n2}.{r}{p}The police investigation concluded that a burglar or someone must have broken in.
There wasn't any money or anything of value here, and I can't imagine a burglar coming to a place like this on a blizzard night.
There's also a rumor that someone used a large sum of money and threats to hush the case up.”
Could that someone be {n2}'s grandfather, the big landowner?
I glanced at {n2}, but she seemed to be thinking of something else.
“...And then,
what happened to that Ichiro person?”
Mr. Mikimoto hesitated for a moment, but finally resolved to speak.
“...The day after his murdered wife's funeral, he was found hanging in the woods over there.”
The hand of {n2} that was gripping mine tightened with such force that it felt like bones would break.
I bore the pain desperately.
Compared to the pain in {n2}'s heart, this was nothing...
A hollow veil had fallen over her eyes, as if to shield her from an unbearable reality.
Not yet.{r}{p}The real shock and sorrow haven't come yet...
Mr. Kobayashi glared sharply at Mr. Mikimoto and said in a voice trembling with anger:
“You...
just who are you?!{r}{p}Spouting that occult writer nonsense.
You're surely one of those scandal-mongers for some photo tabloid.
Is it that fun to dig up old incidents and rub people's nerves raw?!
Get out!”
“Even if you tell me to get out, leaving now is hardly feasible.{r}{p}And I really did begin investigating with the intention of writing an occult article.
Of course, I have my fair share of ambition.

If I could uncover a long-forgotten unsolved case and lead it to a resolution...{r}{p}That would be a feather in my cap, and as a minor member of the press, you could even call it my duty, couldn't you?”
The two glared at each other for a while.
But that lasted only until {n2} shook off my hand and ran out of the room.
On the other side of the door, the girls, who apparently hadn't gone back to their room, were huddled together.
Shoving the startled girls aside, {n2} ran off.
I tried to chase her, but I couldn't help saying one thing first.
“Could you have shown a little...
a little consideration?!{r}{p}Like that...
like that, she...”
I couldn't get any further.
I gave up and chased after {n2}.
{n2} had dashed into her room.
I went to the door and rattled the knob, but it was locked and wouldn't open.
I knocked hard and called out.
You're in there, right?
Let me in!”
“...Leave me alone.”
A surprisingly calm voice came back.
“It's okay.
Just leave me alone for a while.”
If she put it like that, there was nothing to be done.{r}{p}I decided to back off quietly.
When I turned around, not only the office ladies but even Mr. Kobayashi, Mr. Mikimoto and Mr. Kayama were staring at us.
I didn't feel like talking to anyone, so I decided to go back to my own room and called out to {n2} inside.
“Then I'll be in my room.{r}{p}Come whenever you feel like it.{r}{p}Okay?”
There was no answer, but she definitely heard me.
Avoiding everyone's eyes, I went back to my room.
Lying on the bed, I replayed that unbelievable story.
{n2} had real parents who were different, and they had met a tragic death.
And it might have been her grandfather who had her real mother and her parents killed...!
I couldn't even imagine how {n2} felt, suddenly hearing something like this.
I couldn't sit still, so I stood and paced around the room.
I wanted to be by her side.
No, I should leave her alone.
But...
How much time had passed like that?
The sound of shattering glass snapped me back to myself.
Had a window broken?
I opened the door, stuck my head out, and looked around the hallway.
Several people were poking their heads out in the same way.
Mr. Kayama, Mr. Mikimoto, the office ladies...
But {n2}'s door and the door of the man called Tanaka remained closed.
“What happened?”
I called out, but no one could answer.
I ran to {n2}'s room first.
Is it your room?”
No answer.
Turning around, I saw Mr. Kobayashi and his wife and the two part-timers coming up from downstairs.
“What was that sound?”
Mr. Kobayashi asked me.
“I don't know!
But {n2} isn't answering...”
That was the moment.
A scream full of terror and agony rang out, and we froze on the spot.
It was a man's voice.
The only man who wasn't here now...
was the one called Tanaka.
Perhaps used to situations like this, the first to move was, once again, Mr. Mikimoto.
He pounded on the door of Mr. Tanaka's room and called out.
“Are you all right?!
What happened?!”
He tried to open it, but it seemed to be locked.
“Owner!
The master key?
You do have a master key, don't you?{r}{p}Bring it, please!”
Sensing something terribly wrong, Mr. Kobayashi silently ran down the stairs and was back in no time.
Pushing aside Mr. Mikimoto's reaching hand, he unlocked the door himself.
“Mr. Tanaka?
Are you all right?”
Calling out, he opened the door.
In the next moment, snow and wind blasting out from inside made Mr. Kobayashi stagger back two or three steps.
A gust of wind swept down the hallway.
A chill ran down my spine.
It felt as if something that wasn't the wind had passed right by me.
I shook my head, pulled myself together, and approached Mr. Kobayashi and the others.
When the strange gust died down, we all peered inside.
For a moment I thought this room alone had a different interior.
The walls, the ceiling, and even the bed...
everything was patterned like modern art with splashed red paint.
But one look at Mr. Tanaka on the bed made it clear where that paint had come from.
Blood spurting from all over his body, he lay twitching.
“How...
how terrible...”
Mr. Mikimoto was speechless.
There was nothing to be done.
No one could survive losing this much blood.
And in any case, in this blizzard they couldn't even call an ambulance.
While everyone stood frozen, speechless,
Mrs. Kayama clutched her head and collapsed.
“Haruko!
Haruko! Are ya all right?!”
Mr. Kayama hurriedly helped her up.
“...Something...
...something is here...
...it's dangerous...
...all of us...”
She let out a faint murmur, rolled her eyes back, and lost consciousness.
“Please take her to bed.”
Mr. Mikimoto said to Midori, then stepped over to the blood-soaked Mr. Tanaka himself.
He checked the wounds and took his wrist to feel for a pulse.
“...It's no use.”
Trying not to look at the bed, I approached and spoke.
what on earth happened?”
It was pointless to ask Mr. Mikimoto, but I couldn't keep from saying it.
He silently stared at the broken window.
Snow and wind blowing in made the curtains flutter.
“Did something come from there and slash him to pieces...?”
He said as if asking himself.
“S-something?
...Something, what exactly?”
I realized my mouth had gone completely dry.
“I don't know.
It might be what you two saw outside the window.{r}{p}Thinking commonsensically, a human or an animal.”
“An animal?
An animal did this?”
“A ferocious bird of prey, or something like a wolf, maybe.”
Since this was the second floor, a bird seemed more likely, but no matter how sharp a beak, I couldn't imagine it tearing a person to shreds like this.
Mr. Mikimoto continued.
“But judging by the look of it, these aren't that kind of wounds.{r}{p}You couldn't cut flesh this deep without a sharp blade like a knife.”
“...Then it's a human after all.”
“Thinking commonsensically, yes.”
A strange way to put it.
I asked back.
“Then, thinking non-commonsensically?”
After a moment of silence, Mr. Mikimoto said:
“...An evil spirit.”
“An evil spirit?”
“A curse,
you might even say.{r}{p}You remember the story from earlier?{r}{p}Blood has been shed here by several people in the past.{r}{p}The blood of the bitter and unresolved.”
Ridiculous!
...I wanted to retort, but I couldn't.
In front of this horrifying corpse, no such words would come.
Suddenly I remembered {n2}.
What could it mean that she hadn't shown herself despite all this commotion?
Fleeing from the corpse, I rushed out and went back to {n2}'s room.
I knocked even harder than before and called her name.
{n2}! What's wrong?{r}{p}Answer me!”
I was turning to ask Mr. Kobayashi for the master key when it happened.
With a click, the door swung wide open.
“...Is that you, {n1}?
Don't make such a racket.”
{n2} peeked out with a towel wrapped around her head.
Are you okay?
What were you doing?”
“What do you mean...
I was taking a shower.”
Calming down and looking at {n2}, I saw she was wrapped in nothing but a single bath towel.
...My heart skipped a beat.
“...Did something
happen?”
Seeing people in the hall, {n2} asked, covering up.
I was more worried about what the towel hid.
“N-no,
it's nothing serious.”
Saying so, I tried to peek down at her chest from above.
I was almost about to see her cleavage.
“Hey,
something happened, didn't it?
Don't hide it from me.”
I remembered Mr. Tanaka.
“Right!
...Don't be shocked when you hear this.{r}{p}That man called Tanaka seems to have been killed.{r}{p}And in a horrible way.”
{n2}'s eyes went round with fear and shock.
killed?
Wh-
by whom?”
“I don't know.
I don't even know if it was human.{r}{p}When I heard the scream and rushed in, there was no one there, and a human wouldn't have torn him up like that...”
“Torn...
up?”
{n2} covered her mouth with both hands.
“...It seems something came in through the window.{r}{p}That writer, Mikimoto, says it might be an animal.”
Partly because I didn't want to believe an evil spirit had done it, I told her that lie.
“An animal...?
A bear, maybe...{r}{p}They say hungry bears that can't hibernate sometimes attack people...”
“Yeah!
That must be it!”
I decided to ignore the question of how a bear could get to the second floor.
“...That's scary.
I wonder if Uncle has a hunting rifle or something.”
“Who knows.”
If the opponent was neither bear nor human, would a hunting rifle even be of any use?
Thinking that only made my anxiety worse.
“I understand it's a shock, but whatever the case, you'd better stay with everyone.”
{n2} managed a weak smile.
“Okay.
Thanks for worrying about me.{r}{p}I'll come down once I'm dressed.”
“Got it.
If anything happens, shout right away.{r}{p}And I think you'd better not lock the door.”
“Got it.”
